Subject: [ALERT] Meditech: sustained throughput drop in dedicated pool

Team —

Monitoring flagged a sustained ~40% throughput degradation (p95 latency spiking) across Meditech's dedicated GPU pool beginning ~01:50 UTC. Errors are mostly timeouts to runtime workers and increased model evictions. Customers reporting degraded end-user experience.

Quick facts:
- Affected: Meditech production dedicated pool (region-us-west)
- Start: ~2028-01-14 01:50 UTC
- Impact: increased p95 latency, some failed requests (~2.3% of calls)
- Initial hypothesis: node-level memory pressure leading to GPU evictions or driver instability

I've attached a small log snippet from the bridge host (incident-bridge-log-snippet.txt). Launching internal bridge now. Vivek — can you own exec comms? Michael, please lead mitigation. Priyom, grab on-call for routing/scale playbook. Grace, prep a holding statement for the customer.

Laura

Date: 2028-01-14T03:00:00Z
Subject: Re: [ALERT] Meditech: sustained throughput drop in dedicated pool

Diagnostics update: initial root-cause signal points at recent GPU driver patch on the dedicated hosts (kernel driver 540.22) combined with tighter per-process memory limits introduced in last week's config change. The sequence we're seeing: memory pressure -> kernel OOM on user-space driver -> transient worker evictions -> increased latency and timeouts.

Immediate mitigations applied (starting now):
- Rolling restart of 3 affected hosts with the previous stable driver (540.18).
- Temporarily increased per-process memory limit on the dedicated pool.
- Enabled fallback routing to the reserved overflow pool (warm) for Meditech traffic.

I've attached a draft postmortem with preliminary timeline (postmortem-draft-v1.docx). We need to keep the customer informed that we have mitigation in place and are monitoring impact. Expect visible improvement within ~20–30 minutes after restarts and routing shift.

Michael Grant
Director, Runtime Engineering | Redwood Inference

Elena / Jordan —

I want to provide an operational update on the service degradation you reported earlier this morning. Our engineers determined a driver-related instability affecting a subset of hosts in your dedicated GPU pool. We have taken the following actions: 

- Applied rolling restarts to the affected hosts using the validated driver build.
- Increased per-process memory limits to reduce eviction pressure.
- Temporarily routed Meditech traffic to a warmed overflow pool to reduce latency and failures.

Current status: your p95 latency has reduced from the peak and failed requests are down from ~2.3% to ~0.2% in the last 15 minutes. We are continuing to monitor and will keep this routing in place while we validate stability.

Next steps and timeline:
- 04:30 UTC: finish verification window (observe 30-minute stability).
- 06:00 UTC: complete host validation and return traffic to primary pool if stable.
- Within 24 hours: follow-up postmortem with root cause, action items, and compensatory considerations.

Attachments: customer-summary-slide.pdf (one-page operational summary).

We know this interrupted end-user flows and apologize for the disruption. We are committed to a full remediation and will follow up with a detailed postmortem and a proposal for mitigations (including test gating for driver rollouts and expanded warm pool capacity).

Please reply here if you'd like a short briefing call; we can join immediately.

Best,
